# Reading Order Recovery in Two-Column Scientific PDFs
<!-- block p.1 p.1 col=full bbox=[56.0,60.4,457.8,75.4] -->
*A. Author, B. Author (Institute of Document Engineering)*
<!-- block p.1 p.1 col=L bbox=[56.0,84.6,292.6,94.1] -->
> Abstract. We study how a layout-aware reader restores column order in two-column papers and keeps every sentence anchored to the page and block it came from.
<!-- block p.1 p.1 col=full bbox=[56.0,105.4,370.1,113.9] -->

## 1  Introduction
<!-- block p.1 p.1 col=L bbox=[56.0,141.5,132.4,152.5] -->

Two-column papers set text in narrow columns, so one paragraph is split across two frames. A stream-order reader glues right onto left, and turns two sentences into one line.
<!-- block p.1 p.1 col=L bbox=[56.0,158.6,255.0,168.1] -->

The damage is silent: every word is there.
<!-- block p.1 p.1 col=L bbox=[56.0,204.6,231.8,214.1] -->

## 2  Method
<!-- block p.1 p.1 col=L bbox=[56.0,281.5,107.3,292.5] -->

We group characters into lines by baseline, then find vertical gutters from line spans. Lines that cross a gutter become separators. The rest are sorted column by column.
<!-- block p.1 p.1 col=L bbox=[56.0,298.6,237.6,308.1] -->

**Table 1: Spliced lines and order accuracy.**
<!-- block p.1 p.1 col=L bbox=[56.0,353.8,205.0,361.8] -->

| Layout | Spliced | Order acc. |
|---|---|---|
| Two-column (stream order) | 5 | 0.61 |
| Two-column + skill | 0 | 0.98 |
| Single column (control) | 1 | 0.55 |
<sub>table pages [1, 2], table-1</sub>
<!-- block p.1 p.1 col=L bbox=[56.0,368.0,290.0,396.0] -->

Gutter detection alone is not enough: a title, a caption or a wide table breaks the page into bands that must be ordered separately. We segment first, then order inside each band. Every block keeps its page and bounding box.
<!-- block p.1 p.1 col=R bbox=[305.0,158.6,488.8,168.1] -->

**Figure 1: Bands split by a spanning title.**
<!-- block p.1 p.1 col=R bbox=[305.0,261.8,446.8,269.8] -->

<!-- block p.1 p.1 col=L bbox=[56.0,26.2,183.6,33.7] -->

<!-- block p.1 p.1 col=L bbox=[56.0,740.2,314.6,747.7] -->

<!-- block p.1 p.1 col=R bbox=[295.5,795.0,300.5,804.0] -->

### Page 2

## 3  Results and Discussion
<!-- block p.2 p.2 col=full bbox=[223.1,62.7,371.9,74.7] -->

**Table 1 (continued)**
<!-- block p.2 p.2 col=L bbox=[56.0,90.2,120.6,97.7] -->

The stream reader splices five lines here, which is the common word-processor failure. Band segmentation removes every splice. The remaining cost is one pass over the spans.
<!-- block p.2 p.2 col=L bbox=[56.0,142.6,229.7,152.1] -->

Evidence is a page number plus a bounding box, so a reviewer can check the sentence in place. Table rows keep the header of their first page. Formulas keep number and script structure.
<!-- block p.2 p.2 col=R bbox=[305.0,142.6,510.4,152.1] -->

```
S = αx^{2} + βy_{−1}  (2)
```
